title: kbu model: RAST auto-annotation on reconstruct, and GLPK as the configurable default solver

summary: Fixes two measured defects in the kbu model arc. (1) reconstruct returns a 5-reaction template scaffold at exit 0 from a 4,285-protein E. coli FASTA because MSGenome.from_fasta leaves MSFeature.ontology_terms empty and MSBuilder maps genes only via ontology_terms['RAST'] -- fixed by a new annotate_msgenome adapter over the existing RastUtils AnnotatorUtils, driven by a tri-state --annotate auto|always|never, with a HARD ERROR (never a silent scaffold) when annotation is needed and unreachable. (2) gapfill dies with 'Model too large for size-limited license' because nothing in KBUtilLib ever sets a cobra solver, so optlang picks a restricted commercial licence ahead of GLPK -- fixed by --solver on all four verbs resolving explicit > KBU_SOLVER > modeling.solver in ~/.kbutillib/config.yaml > glpk, with h100 overriding via its own per-machine config file and no hostname detection anywhere.

key_decisions.annotation_trigger: measured absence (is_annotated() False), never inferred from file type/extension; --annotate auto|always|never, default auto
key_decisions.annotation_failure: HARD ERROR -- reconstruct fails and names the missing annotation; the scaffold is reachable only via explicit --annotate never. The replaced behaviour was exit 0 on a broken result, which is why it survived
key_decisions.annotator_choice: KBUtilLib RastUtils (AnnotatorUtils) via a thin adapter, NOT modelseedpy's one-line RastClient.annotate_genome -- buys structured RastServiceError, configurable timeout, chunking, protein guard, and lets bakta/prokka drop in later
key_decisions.no_sso_translation: MSBuilder consumes raw RAST role strings directly via normalize_role; translate_rast_function_to_sso / convert_role_to_searchrole are NOT on this path. An entire subsystem the prior session expected is unnecessary
key_decisions.solver_default: glpk, in code as DEFAULT_SOLVER -- not in the repo's root config.yaml, which _find_config_file resolves at priority 3 and would leak to every machine
key_decisions.solver_precedence: explicit --solver > KBU_SOLVER env > modeling.solver from ~/.kbutillib/config.yaml > glpk; one resolve_solver() shared by the CLI and the library constructors
key_decisions.solver_config_trap: get_config_value is INERT on the kbu model CLI path -- _construct_offline passes config_file=False, _config_hash is {}, and get_config_value has no env fallback. So the CLI reads ~/.kbutillib/config.yaml DIRECTLY via a helper shaped like the existing _resolve_modelseed_db_path(). Pinned by a regression test
key_decisions.h100_override: h100's own ~/.kbutillib/config.yaml sets modeling.solver: gurobi. Per-machine by construction; no hostname detection, no fleet topology in the library
key_decisions.solver_application: apply_solver sets BOTH cobra.Configuration().solver (before any model is built or loaded) and model.solver on the held model. Neither is redundant: cobra resolves global config at model-construction time
key_decisions.no_solver_fallback: an unavailable solver raises, naming the resolved name and its precedence source. Silent cross-solver fallback is how the original defect stayed invisible
key_decisions.no_import_side_effect: library default is set in MSReconstructionUtils/MSFBAUtils __init__, not at module import. An import that silently changes a caller's solver is a worse surprise
key_decisions.remote_lp_solver: NOT the answer -- ms_remote_solver_utils is an LP-text-in/solution-out HTTP client, not an optlang interface, so it cannot be assigned to cobra.Configuration().solver. And GLPK is measured-sufficient, so the poplar tunnel stays out of the modelling arc's default path
key_decisions.json_schema: additive only -- solver and annotation keys added; model_path/reactions/metabolites/genes unchanged
key_decisions.privacy: auto-annotation makes third-party transmission to tutorial.theseed.org the DEFAULT of the most-run verb on a Berkeley-operated pod. Mitigated by a mandatory stderr disclosure on every annotating run plus --annotate never; NO sensitive-data guard was built (named, not silently omitted)
key_decisions.kbhub_validation: kbhub is not a Maestro worker and has no maestro client, so NO taskplan task can run there. The plan carries tests that pass anywhere; the pod end-to-end run is an Albert acceptance step OUTSIDE the plan, asserting numbers (reconstruct >500 reactions AND >500 genes; gapfill non-empty reactions_added; FBA objective_value > 0) -- never exit codes
key_decisions.taskplan_shape: 5 sequential single-task phases, not parallel groups: load_taskplan rejects a parallel_group whose tasks share a repo, because concurrent branches in one repo collide

ms_solver_config (precedence table; empty-value fallthrough; apply to global and to model)
